_comment: Events. One list, newest first -- there is no separate 'past' list, because the website works out what is upcoming from the date and sorts them itself. The order here does not matter. 'date' must be YYYY-MM-DD. 'registerUrl' is optional; leave it empty and the Register button does not appear, and it stops being offered on its own once the date has passed. Leave a blank line between paragraphs in a description and the page will lay them out as paragraphs; the list shows the first sentence or two and links to the rest.

events.title: Sharing the Spirit: Reflections on America's 250th
events.address: 51 South San Antonio Road, Los Altos, CA 94022
events.description:
A summer history event marking 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence, held with the Los Altos History Museum.

We meet at the museum for a private viewing of its special exhibit, “The Spirit of '76 — Reflecting on America's 250”. Amy Ellison, the museum's Director of Exhibits, then speaks about the exhibit and the ideas behind it, and Pamela Baird looks back at Fourth of July celebrations in Mountain View and at how the city marked the Bicentennial through 1976.

There is no charge to attend, but registration is required. Anyone who joins or renews on the day receives a copy of Mary Jo Ignoffo's “Milestones: A History of Mountain View”, which normally sells for $20 at our events.

events.title: Walking Tour of Historic Downtown Mountain View
events.address: 600 West Evelyn Avenue, Mountain View, CA 94041
events.description:
Step into history with a guided walking tour of historic downtown Mountain View. Our volunteers lead you along Castro Street through more than 150 years of the city's development — the buildings that survive, the ones that did not, and the people behind both. The route is about a mile and takes around two hours.

We meet at the metal arch on the corner of Castro Street and Evelyn Avenue. Suggested donation $10 for members, $15 for everyone else. Places are limited, so registration is required.

events.title: Winter Quarterly Event: Italians of Mountain View
events.description:
Families, founders, friendships — the story of Italian immigration to Mountain View.

The talk follows Italian families from their arrival in the Bay Area in the 1850s to their move south into Mountain View: the Armaninis, the Mancinis and others, the Italian-American mayors who served the city, and the restaurants and food businesses that are still part of downtown.

events.title: More than Orchards: Mountain View in Gilded Age America, 1880–1920
events.description:
Nancy Unger's richly illustrated talk sets Mountain View against the wider changes of the Gilded Age, treating the town as a mirror of what was happening to California and to the country between 1880 and 1920.

Along the way: the railroad and the technologies that followed it, the waves of immigration that shaped the valley, specialty crops and the money they brought, political reform, what people did for pleasure, and the women's clubs and suffrage campaigns that changed who had a say.

events.title: Disasters of Mountain View: Earthquakes, Fires & Airplane Crashes
events.description:
Mountain View and its residents have lived through two major earthquakes, more fires than anyone can easily count, and several tragic aeroplane crashes.

This talk gathers those events together and asks what each one did to the town — what was lost, what was rebuilt, and how the city changed its mind about building, water and fire in the years that followed.
